claims.text: Atomic layer deposition of platinum-group metals on high-surface-area supports can improve catalytic activity.
Atomic layer deposition of platinum-group metals on high-surface-area supports can improve catalyst durability.
Atomic layer deposition can reduce platinum-group-metal consumption in automotive exhaust catalysts.
The intervention is atomic layer deposition of platinum-group metals.
The proposed effect applies in high-temperature exhaust gas containing reducing and oxidizing agents.
High-surface-area supports serve as the structural mediator of the intervention.
Atomic layer deposition increases the dispersion of platinum-group metals.
Atomic layer deposition increases utilization of platinum-group metals.
Atomic layer deposition enhances catalyst thermal stability.
The intervention will improve catalytic activity by 20% relative to a conventional catalyst without atomic layer deposition.
The intervention will reduce platinum-group-metal consumption by 30% relative to a conventional catalyst without atomic layer deposition.
The intervention will increase durability by 25% relative to a conventional catalyst without atomic layer deposition.
The predicted effects should hold from 500 to 900 degrees Celsius.
The predicted effects should hold at platinum-group-metal loadings of 0.1 to 1.0 g/L.
